chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Bureyd al-Ijli, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he had broken his fast during the month of Ramadan for three days. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is asked,

He is asked, "Is there a sin upon you regarding your breaking the fast during the month of Ramadan?" So if he says, "No", then it is upon the Imam to kill him; and if he says, "Yes", then it is upon the Imam to flog him.

key_terms.يَنْهَكَهُ: He flogs him / He strikes him

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for breaking fast if one denies the sin versus admitting it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the judicial mechanism of *ikhrāj* (eliciting confession) used by the Imam to determine the penalty for deliberate fasting violation. It distinguishes between *qatl* (execution) for those who deny the sin, implying a higher degree of culpability or *hudud* severity, and *nahk* (corporal punishment) for those who admit, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential nuance between fixed punishments and discretionary penalties.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Bureyd Al Ijaly who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he had broken a Fast during the Month of Ramazan for three days. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be asked, ‘Is there a sin upon you regarding your breaking the Fast during the Month of Ramazan?’

So if he says, ‘No’, then it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> kills him; and if he says, ‘Yes’, so it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> reprimands him by lashes’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Burayd al- ‘ Ij liy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man against whom witnesses testify that he has destroyed his fast of the month of Ramadan for three days. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is asked, ‘Is there a sin upon you because of destroying your fast of the month of Ramadan?’
If he says, ‘No, there is no sin,’ then it is the responsibility of the Imam to execute him. If he says, ‘Yes, there is sin, then it is the responsibility of the Imam to reprimand him.”’
